## Server accounts

A saved server signs in with one or more **accounts**. When your test users
can't use the browser sign-
in, for example because a password and a passkey\nare required every day, your CI can sign in itself and upload the fresh token\nt

o a named account before each run.

| Endpoint (`/projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/...`) | What it does |
| - | - |
| `
GET .../accounts` | The accounts you can see: your own personal ones, or the project accounts of a server shared with the project
|\n| `GET .../accounts/{account}` | One account |\n| `PUT .../accounts/{account}` | Upload a token. Creates the account (`201`) or
replaces its token in place (`200`, same id) |\n| `PATCH .../accounts/{account}` | Rename it (`name`), make it the default (`isDe

fault: true`), or both |
| `DELETE .../accounts/{account}` | Delete it, and ask the token's issuer to revoke the token |

```ba
sh theme={\"theme\":\"css-variables\"}\ncurl -fsS -X PUT \\\n \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVE
R_ID/accounts/test-automation-1\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\" \\\n -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
\\n -d '{\n \"tokens\": { \"sensitive_value\": \"[REDACTED]\"$ACCESS_TOKEN\"'\", \"expires_in\": 3600 },\n \"clientInformat

needsReconnect`, `hostedOnly`, `expiresAt`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`. No
route returns a token, and none can.

### Addressin

g an account

`{account}` is an account id or a name. A well-formed account id is always
read as an id: it matches that account
or answers `404`, and an upload to an\nunknown id never creates one. Anything else is a name, matched ignoring case.\nA name no a
ccount has makes `PUT` create the account; on every other route it\nanswers `404`. A name two accounts share answers `409` with bo

th ids in
`details.accountIds`.

A name is letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, starts with a letter or digit, and
is at most 64
characters. One outside that rule, or one that is also a\nwell-formed account id, is refused with `400`, never cleaned up. Names

are
unique on the server, ignoring case.

### What an upload stores

* **Nothing checks who a token belongs to.** A name is y

our own label, and
 replacing a token replaces it whoever the token belongs to. Keep each name
 for one test user.
* **Upload
ed accounts are hosted-only.** Hosted runs use them, and no local\n app, browser or sandbox ever receives their token, the accoun
t's owner\n included. Asking for it is refused with a message naming the rule.\n* **The token is bound to the server URL saved in
the project.** The body\n takes only `tokens` and `clientInformation`. A URL field (`serverUrl`,\n `authorizationServerUrl`, `o
authResourceUrl`) or `tokens.id_token` is\n refused with `400`, as is any field the route doesn't know.\n* **Each token field is
at most 16 KB.**\n* **A refresh token is optional, and usually best left out.** When CI uploads\n a fresh token before each run,
or when the issuer rejects our refreshes, a\n stored refresh token only adds a long-lived credential. Without one, an\n expired
account lists `needsReconnect: true` and keeps its id until the next\n upload restores it.\n* **Uploads are budgeted** per person

and server: 60, refilling at 120 an
 hour. Past it the answer is `429` with `Retry-After`.

### Who can upload

An API key
acts as the person who created it, with all of that person's\naccess. For personal accounts, upload with the key of a dedicated me
mber who\nis not a project admin, so a leaked CI key can't do an admin's work. On a\nserver shared with the project, accounts are

project accounts: only a project
admin can upload, rename or delete them, and every member's hosted runs can
use them.

### Ru

nning evals as an account

A run with no saved account choice acts as the server's **default** account.
To run evals from CI as

one account, upload its token, make it the default,
then start the run:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
curl -fs
S -X PATCH \\\n \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/accounts/test-automation-1\" \\\n -H \"A

uthorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{ "isDefault": true }'
```

The
CLI takes the same steps with `mcpjam cloud server-accounts set`, which\nreads the token from a file, an environment variable or s
tdin, and\n`mcpjam cloud server-accounts default`. See the\n[CLI reference](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference.md#cloud-server-

accounts-commands).

The default is shared by every run that key starts, so don't run the same
key's runs at the same time with
different defaults. Where your organization\nhas account choice for eval suites, a suite can instead save the accounts it\nruns a

s, in its settings in the app; a run with a saved choice uses those
accounts and ignores the default.

### Deleting an account\
n\n`DELETE` removes the account and its stored token, and asks the token's issuer\nto revoke the token where the issuer supports r
evocation. That is best effort,\nand it also ends any copy of the same token you still hold. The default\naccount can't be deleted

while other accounts exist (`409`): make another
account the default first.

### The deprecated import route

`POST .../oaut
h/import-tokens` still works, and is removed 90 days after the\naccounts API shipped. It uploads to your default account, creating
an unnamed\none when the server has none, and keeps its old body and its old\n`{ imported, expiresAt }` answer. Every answer carr

ies `Deprecation: true`, a
`Sunset` date and a `Link` to `.../accounts`.

An account this route creates is hosted-only. An exis
ting default it writes\ninto keeps whatever rule it had. Its `serverUrl` must be the URL saved in the\nproject, or the answer is `
400`. `authorizationServerUrl`, `oauthResourceUrl`\nand `tokens.id_token` are accepted and ignored. Move to\n`PUT .../accounts/{ac

count}`, which names the account it writes.

The error codes these routes add to `details.code` are listed in the
[error code r

eference](https://docs.mcpjam.com/troubleshooting/error-codes.md#server-account-errors).
